text:
nisha: FYI discovered parity bug in .NET SDK during onboarding e2e. API accepts timeout as integer seconds but .NET sends TimeSpan string and server returns 400.

nisha: repro: REST vs SDK payloads:
curl -> {"model":"gpt-xyz","input":"hi","timeout":30}
.dotnet -> {"model":"gpt-xyz","input":"hi","timeout":"00:00:30"}

tom: yep, System.Text.Json serializes TimeSpan as hh:mm:ss by default. Server validation expects number (secs) or ms.

ben: impact: PLG quickstart and any customers using .NET will see validation errors on inference calls when they set timeouts.

courtney: options: add JsonConverter<TimeSpan> to emit seconds (non-breaking) OR change model to expose int TimeoutSeconds (breaking). Recommend converter + tests.

ben: agree. add a small contract test that posts sample objects (timeout, priority, batch_size) from each SDK to catch drift.

ci-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/dotnet-sdk/pull/68 - adds TimeSpan -> seconds converter and unit test. CI: formatting check failing.

nisha: workaround: call RawPost with prebuilt JSON or set timeout in seconds via raw body. Patched nuget validated on staging / hotfix pending.

ci-bot: Release job queued for dotnet-sdk v1.3.1 (hotfix).

nisha: staging verification ✅. closing thread.
